newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-JAGGE WINS SLALOM, ALPHAND IS OVERALL CHAMPION.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-JAGGE WINS SLALOM, ALPHAND IS OVERALL CHAMPION.

text.p: Finn Christian Jagge of Norway won the men's slalom in the final race of the World Cup season that also brought an historic overall championship crown to Luc Alphand of France.
Alphand became the first Frenchman in 29 years, since Jean-Claude Killy, to win the overall title and the first speed specialist ever to capture the championship.
The 31-year-old Frenchman clinched the crystal globe when his only rival, Kjetil Andre Aamodt of Norway, failed to finish first or second in the climactic slalom.
Aamodt, the 1994 World Cup champion, finished seventh.

Jagge, who led by 0.72 of a second after a brilliant first run, won his first race of the season with a combined time of one minute, 37.94 seconds, 0.12 of a second faster than Austrian Thomas Stangassinger.
Italian star Alberto Tomba took third place in 1:38.19, 0.25 of a second off the pace.
In fourth place was Austrian Mario Reiter, who officially knocked Aamodt out of the overall race when he posted his time of 1:38.49.

Thomas Sykora of Austria, who finished ninth in the race, won the season slalom title over Stangassinger. Sebastian Amiez of France finished 18th and last in the race but held on to third in the slalom standings.
